sense.text: Today’s class is sealing the 144,000. “And I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a book written within and on the backside, sealed with seven seals”: we went over this before. This is in the heavens; the Father has a book with seven seals on it, and no one can open the seals except Christ.

“I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held”: there are Israelites who have already been sealed from way back. The apostles and those loyal men that followed them were sealed, and some of the prophets; these are the souls you are reading about here.

“How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?”: this shows you that the souls of the righteous speak to the Lord. The Lord don’t want to hear the wicked. It is only the righteous he gives ear to, those that gave their lives for this truth.

“That they should rest yet for a little season”: this little season is the season we are living in right now. We are in the fifth seal. “Until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled”: that does not mean everybody that follows the law is going to be put to death.

precepts.why: “And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him”: that’s what our people are doing on earth, and in the spirit realm those that have died are doing the same thing. Christ commanded us to pray for vengeance against our enemies.

“And some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues”: some does not mean all. Just as it was back then, so shall it be today; some are allotted to be killed in this truth.

sense.text: “And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”: we want to examine what these four winds make reference to. It is not regular wind, because regular wind blows on the earth, on the sea and on trees. The wind makes reference to the armies of the nations scattered throughout the four corners.
“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”: now we examine his seal.
“Till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads”: what’s behind your forehead is your mind. That’s what the sealing is all about, being sealed in our mind, our understanding.

precepts.why: “A multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”: these are the nations of men who want to fight against Christ, the man that came out of the sea. What comes from those four winds is military men: army, navy, air forces and marines.
What is this seal talking about? “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.”
“But he that giveth his mind to the law of the most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.”
“I will put my laws into their mind”: putting his law in our minds is what the seal makes reference to.

An example of the sealing in the Old Testament. The word for seal in this chapter is mark, and it don’t mean tattoo. This is during the time of the Babylonian onslaught, as they began to destroy Jerusalem. The six men with slaughter weapons and the man clothed with linen are angels, and they represent what Babylon is about to do; the angels were controlling the minds of Babylon, kill this one, spare that one. “Set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof”: the Lord is telling them to seal his servants that are in Jerusalem. “Go ye after him through the city, and smite”: for the rest of the Israelites that are not sealed, kill. “But come not near any man upon whom is the mark”: anyone that is sealed, don’t slay them, so our foreparents were being sealed even back then. “And begin at my sanctuary”: why not start with the drug dealer first? Because it is in the sanctuary that we are supposed to be following the laws of the Most High; they are supposed to know better. “And I was left”: Ezekiel was left because he was marked. “For they say, The Lord hath forsaken the earth, and the Lord seeth not”: our people were saying the Lord don’t see my wickedness.
We be waiting for 12,000 of each tribe; it is not going to be like that, some have already been sealed. “Who hath also sealed us”: Paul is a part of that us.
“After that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise.”
“Whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption”: meaning the second coming. Many of the foreparents were already sealed, so don’t hold your breath waiting for 12,000 of each tribe.

sense.text: “Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women”: you got to wonder why the Lord put women off to the side like that. Some of these little children are not right; they are so cute and so adorable, but they are evil. And women: let me show you something about women that’s going to happen.

precepts.why: “There came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said unto him, Go up, thou bald head”: go up means get out of here. Little children have no filter. For the prophet to curse them in the name of the Lord, he was mad, because these little children were evil. “And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them”: a she bear with cubs is worse than the male, relentless. God didn’t just send any bears, he sent two she bears.

This sister was about manipulation and contradiction; she is the American-minded woman. “She painted her face, and tired her head”: there is nothing wrong with painting the face, women did it all throughout the Bible, but sometimes it looks like witchcraft, because that’s not the real them. Let him fall in love with the real you. “Throw her down. So they threw her down: and some of her blood was sprinkled on the wall”; “and he trode her under foot.” “But they found no more of her than the skull, and the feet, and the palms of her hands.” “In the portion of Jezreel shall dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel.” Brothers used to ask why Elijah, after calling fire down, ran from Jezebel. Elijah had no power over Jezebel, because God had already prophesied how she was going to die and by whose hand, and it was not him.

But sister, we ain’t going to leave you on the side of the road like that; we want to save you from being thrown out of a window. “Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing”: when women read that, they say I just had a baby, so I’m safe. No; many wicked women out in the world are having babies, and they are not going to be saved. “If they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety”: if is a two-letter word with a big meaning. Charity means you got to love your neighbour like you love yourself.

This is what being saved in childbearing goes back to, a verse many American women despise. “In sorrow thou shalt bring forth children”: the childbearing pains, and the cramps every month. “And thy desire shall be to thy husband”: this is the desire you women must have to be saved. “And he shall rule over thee”: that’s the judgment. Childbearing doesn’t just mean having babies; she remembers why she suffers the pains, for being disobedient to the Lord.

“I came not to send peace, but a sword.” “And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household”: brothers that are so desperate to get married better meditate on verse 36. Christ is letting you know you are going to have enemies in your house, whether mother, father, wife or children. “He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me.”

sense.text: “And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”: only the Israelites are being sealed.

“Of the tribe of Juda were sealed twelve thousand”: Judah is the first tribe raised up in understanding. “Of the tribe of Reuben”: the Seminole Indians. In the early stages, in the 1400s, they wore the mitre, not the feathered headdress. “Of the tribe of Gad”: the American Indians.

“Of the tribe of Issachar were sealed twelve thousand”: there has been a lot of hatred against Issachar. Brothers are bringing hatred from gang wars in LA and the prison system into the truth to justify Issachar not being Israel; that’s false. An old book, Origin of the American Indians, says the Mexicans are originally of the ten tribes captured by Shalmaneser, and of the family of Issachar. They are Israelites. The Spanish caste chart sorted the Indians into categories by who married who, which is why Paul said to avoid endless genealogies.

“Of the tribe of Zabulon were sealed twelve thousand”: from Guatemala down towards Panama, the Mayans. “Of the tribe of Joseph”: people get simple and say it says Joseph, not Ephraim, but Joseph makes reference to Ephraim. “Of the tribe of Benjamin”: the so-called West Indians, Jamaica, Trinidad, the Bahamas. We never taught that the twelve tribes are only in the Western Hemisphere; that is a narrative they are trying to put out there.

precepts.why: The prophet Esdras saw a similar vision. “Behold the number of those that be sealed”: that’s the 144. “Take thy number, O Sion, and shut up those of thine that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the law of the Lord”: seal them with what? It tells you right there, which have fulfilled the law of the Lord. “May be hallowed”: made holy.

The question often comes from the Christian woman who comes into the truth: is she part of the 144? No. “And with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads”: the Father’s name in their minds. “These are they which were not defiled with women”: that’s how you know the 144 is not female. That does not mean they are not married; Peter and many of the apostles and prophets had wives. It goes back to philosophies that often come from women, like Eve bringing a doctrine to Adam, or a woman bringing feminism to the man to pull him out of the truth. “For they are virgins”: not corrupted by the philosophies. “These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth”: whatever Christ says, the 144 is going to do it. The 144 is God’s government under Christ.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”: the first tribe raised up in understanding is Judah. “That the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah”: we were always disrespected, and that disrespect is going to stop.

Once Judah gets raised up in their right mind, this is what the tribe of Judah is going to do. “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people”: Judah would have the map, understand where the tribes are and who they are, and go out and gather the people. “And be thou an help to him from his enemies”: when the enemies rise up against Judah, God will help them, even from the time of Martin Luther King.

“He dwelleth as a lion”: when Gad was on this side of the world they were predators on the land. “And teareth the arm with the crown of the head”: that’s the blood brother; to be part of their tribe you went to him who wore the crown, the large feathered bonnet. “And he provided the first part for himself”: North America. “Because there, in a portion of the lawgiver, was he seated”: Gad dealt with the laws on this side of the world. “And he came with the heads of the people”: Ephraim and Manasseh.

Why do some American Indians look so different? “Concerning the Ammonites”: Ammon, the Asians. “Why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?” With the construction of the railroads many Asians were brought over and had children with the American Indians. The darker ones were pushed off the reservations, and Esau moved in and had children. The old photos show the American Indians with straight hair but dark skinned. We are not saying none of them are Gadites; some of them are.

“Neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith”: we can’t determine where everyone’s ancestry goes back to. Watch out for ancestry.com; they can take your DNA and put it wherever they want. Paul said avoid it; just deal with hearing his voice and let God settle out the rest.

“Issachar is a strong ass couching down between two burdens”: the animal symbol is the burro. “And he saw that rest was good”: they honour the siesta. Many South American countries keep the siesta, but Mexico is famous for it.

Issachar and Zebulun are written together because of this verse; look at the map. “Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents”: Issachar, the Aztecs, resided primarily in Mexico, and Zebulun, the Mayans from Guatemala down towards Panama, would go out from their tents to meet Issachar. “For they shall suck of the abundance of the seas, and of treasures hid in the sand.”

“Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea”: the haven of the sea is the Panama Canal. Yes, Benjamin travelled to Panama in the late 1800s and early 1900s to help build the canal, and they intermarried there.

“Then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim”: so when Revelation 7 mentions Joseph, it is talking about Ephraim. The twelve tribes chart comes from here. “And join them one to another into one stick”: that’s the grafting in Paul was talking about, the two kingdoms coming back together as one nation. “Wilt thou not shew us what thou meanest by these?”: the Israelites would see the names of the twelve tribes joined together and ask questions. “And the sticks whereon thou writest shall be in thine hand before their eyes”: Ezekiel walked around with the twelve tribes chart in his hand.

A side note for up and coming scholars. “And thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them”: some say the grafting in is the white man grafted in among us, while they reject Puerto Ricans, Dominicans, Mexicans and Native Indians. That’s white supremacy. The grafting in is based on Ezekiel 37.

There is another one saying the northern kingdom never left Africa. “With them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh”: Ephraim and Manasseh would push the people to the ends of the earth. Is that just Africa?
“When he shall roar, then the children shall tremble from the west”: from the west, not the east. The book of Hosea, the bulk of it, makes reference to the northern kingdom.
“I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west”: how did we get to the west? That’s what the book of 2 Esdras was talking about.
“Behold, I will save my people from the east country”: that’s Africa. “And from the west country”: that’s the Americas, on this side of the world. It is clear as day.

sense.text: “A great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues”: some say this is all races. Verse 9 is not talking about all races; this great multitude of Israel is coming out of all nations. Their argument is Israel was scattered in all nations except Mexico, except Puerto Rico, except Santo Domingo; it makes no sense.
“Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb”: hold that, our God.
“And worshipped God, Saying, Amen: Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever.”

precepts.why: Verse 42 explains Revelation 7:9. “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number”: mount Sion is another name for the Israelites.

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other”: when the Bible says the seed of Israel would be among all nations, it means just that, even among the so-called Jewish people. The clip Little White Lie showed a woman raised as white whose father was a black man. Since the transatlantic slave trade, some of us stayed amongst ourselves, and some of us married in amongst the nations we dwelt among, and some of their looks changed. Not all of them, but some.

You can’t prove who all the tribes are throughout the world; you’re right, we don’t know. Families travel; men went to Vietnam and had babies there, and West Indians intermarried in Panama. It is impossible for us as men to determine who’s who, but there is a God. “I shall set the people in order”: whatever we got wrong, whatever we don’t know, the Lord is going to set the people in order. That’s going to be done in the wilderness.

“And had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”: we joke that a brother thinks he’s going in a gate and the angel says no, that’s not your gate. Order will be set before them gates.

“Salvation to our God”: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else.” Isn’t he the God of everybody? No; the Bible says he is only the God of Israel. This is why they want to get rid of the King James Bible. An article on the Afro-Germans showed that after 1945 soldiers of African descent fathered children in Germany, and thousands were adopted by American families. When the Bible says we are in all nations, it means exactly that.

“Confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them”: among the other nations we are to confess the Lord. “And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again”: that’s why we are on the bottom of society and went through slavery. “And will gather us out of all nations, among whom he hath scattered us”: the deliverance is not for literally all other nations; it is for the Israelites scattered amongst those nations.

sense.text: “What are these which are arrayed in white robes? and whence came they?”: verses 1 to 8 are the leading government of Israel, the 144; some have already died, some are being born in this time period. The great multitude in verse 9 includes other men of Israel, Israelite women and Israelite children. Why didn’t he recognise who they were? Something changed; the way we came out of Egypt is not the way we look now.

“These are they which came out of great tribulation”: in Christian commentaries blacks, Latinos and Native Indians don’t exist. You read that the great tribulation is a seven-year period where two Europeans prophesy and a monster comes from the depths of hell, or seven years where you need a chip in your hand, but you never read about the transatlantic slave trade. The tribulation nobody wants to talk about is slavery, our captivity; that’s the great tribulation, from then until now.
“They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat.”

“And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes”: that is the prophecy regarding our people in the last days. All of the 12,000 of each tribe, whatever that number is, alive now upon earth are being sealed, and all of us are being gathered.

precepts.why: Moses prophesied about great tribulation for the Israelites. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”: the lands we went to, they were killing us by the hundreds of thousands, in the Middle Passage alone. “And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone”: in slavery they forced us to worship their gods; in Iran and Iraq the false god Allah, in the European countries the white image of Jesus. “If thou seek him with all thy heart”: you seek the Lord through the Bible, not through osmosis. “When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days”: what things? Slavery.

Christian commentary makes believe our slavery never existed. “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”: we just saw that in the clip, as the brother fell down because they took his daughter. “And there shall be no might in thine hand”: no military, economic or political might to get our sons and daughters back.
“And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee”: slavery never happened, according to white Christians.

“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”: slavery again, with slave ships. “And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you”: no man shall deliver you from God’s curses.
“They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun smite them: for he that hath mercy on them shall lead them, even by the springs of water shall he guide them.”

Who is this talking about? “Thus saith the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel”: it is amazing for you to read Revelation 7 and get other races out of that. It is talking about the Israelites coming out of other nations.
“And the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.”
